title: Neutron schema document v2
description: Cross-language schema contract shared by the TypeScript exporter and the Go CLI. A document is a single JSON object describing a PostgreSQL schema state (desired or introspected). The shape here is normative for structure; cross-object rules (identity uniqueness, foreign-key resolution, codec/type consistency, capability requirements) are enforced by the reference validators in cli/internal/db and contracts/data/consumer.ts, and pinned by the golden fixtures in contracts/data/golden/. Canonical serialization and hashing are defined by contracts/data/CANONICAL.md. Unknown versions, unknown fields, unknown types and duplicate identities are rejected. Objects this contract cannot represent (extension-owned tables, unsupported catalog structures) are never flattened: they appear only as opaque inventory entries.

version.description: Explicit format version. Documents declaring any other value are rejected with code unknown-version.

dialect.description: SQL dialect the document targets. v2 targets PostgreSQL only.

capabilities.description: Capabilities the document requires (engine extension or Nucleus feature). Unordered set: canonical form sorts it. columns of type vector require pgvector or nucleus here.

schemas.description: SQL namespaces (schema objects). Every identity.schema anywhere in the document must be declared here. Unordered set: canonical form sorts by name.

tables.description: Tables. The array order in the source document is presentation only: the set is unordered for identity and hashing, and canonical form sorts by (schema, name) and sorts each table's constraints and indexes. Ordering that is semantic lives inside ordered tuples (each table's columns, constraint columns, index key parts).

enums.description: Enum types. Field is required even when empty so the shape can represent documents without enums unambiguously. values are an ordered tuple: PostgreSQL enum order is semantic.

views.description: Views. Field is required even when empty. definition is stored verbatim; expression equivalence is a planner concern, not a contract concern.

opaque.description: Read-only inventory of catalog objects this contract cannot represent: extension-owned tables, unsupported structures, external objects. Never flattened into tables. Tools must not generate DDL from these entries.

name.description: Identifier or object name. Must be non-empty and free of control characters (C0 including NUL, and DEL). Quoting rules are the producer's concern; the contract stores names verbatim.

sqlText.description: SQL text (expression, predicate, view definition, reason). Stored and hashed verbatim; must be non-empty and free of NUL. No statement separator is permitted in expression positions (enforced by validators for single expressions).

columnType.description: Column type with parameters and codec metadata. Type names are PostgreSQL pg_catalog typnames (introspection-faithful). Arrays are represented with array: true on the element type description.

name.description: Base type name. enum requires the enum reference field and resolves to a declared enum object.

params.description: Type parameters. Allowed keys per type (enforced by validators): varchar: length; numeric: precision, scale (scale requires precision, scale <= precision); timestamp/timestamptz: precision 0..6; vector: dimensions (required). All values are plain integers.

array.description: True when the column is an array of the base type. When true, codec must be array.

codec.description: Codec metadata: how values of this column are represented on the wire (program README section 3.3). Validators enforce the default codec per type: bool=boolean, int2/int4/float4/float8=number, int8=bigint, numeric=decimal-string, text/varchar=string, timestamp=timestamp-string, timestamptz=timestamptz-string, date=date-string, bytea=binary, uuid=uuid, json/jsonb=json, vector=vector, enum=enum, arrays=array.

sql.description: Exactly one SQL literal token, optionally cast: a single-quoted string (with '' doubling), a numeric literal, true, false or null. Text that looks like an expression (now(), gen_random_uuid()) must be tagged expression instead.

oneOf.description: GENERATED {ALWAYS | BY DEFAULT} AS IDENTITY. Valid only on integer columns (int2/int4/int8).
Sequence-backed default (nextval), the serial representation. Valid only on integer columns. The sequence schema must be declared in schemas.

columnDefault.description: Defaults are tagged values. The tag is authoritative: 'now()' as a literal string and now() as an expression are different documents with different hashes.

column.description: Table column. Absence of default means no default. Primary-key columns must declare notNull: true explicitly (validators reject otherwise; v2 performs no silent normalization). A generated column carries its stored expression in generated and never a default; virtual generated columns are not representable (explicitly unsupported).

generated.description: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expression) STORED. Database-computed; never written.

constraint.description: Table-level constraint. Constraint columns are an ordered tuple: composite key column order is semantic and preserved verbatim by canonicalization.

references.description: Reference target tuples are ordered and name-based: the referenced column names need not match the referencing column names (renamed targets are representable). The target tuple must be covered by a primary-key or unique constraint on the referenced table (validators enforce).

indexDef.description: Index with schema-global identity. key is an ordered tuple of key parts; include is an unordered set (canonical form sorts it).

opclass.description: Explicit operator class (X01). Omitted = the method's default class for the type. pgvector indexes select distance semantics this way (vector_ops / vector_cosine_ops / vector_ip_ops).

oneOf.description: Expression key parts cannot carry per-part ordering: per-part deparse is engine-dependent, so ordered expression keys are explicitly unsupported (validators reject order/nulls here).

key.description: Ordered key parts. Per-part ordering is stored in minimal form (Q07): order is written only for desc (asc is the default), nulls only when it is not the direction default (asc defaults to nulls last, desc to nulls first). This matches what introspection derives from pg_index.indoption, so desired and introspected documents canonicalize identically.

with.description: Access-method parameters (X01): with (m = 16, ef_construction = 64) on hnsw, with (lists = 100) on ivfflat, with (fillfactor = 90) on btree — introspected reloptions round-trip on any method. Integer values only (non-integer reloptions keep the index unrepresentable); the server validates the keys. Canonical form sorts the keys.

managed.description: Managed-scope metadata: whether this object is inside the managed scope of the workflow that produced the document. Desired documents declare their objects managed; introspected documents mark scope explicitly. Never inferred.

columns.description: Ordered tuple: physical column order (PostgreSQL attnum) is part of the schema state. Two documents that differ only in column order are different schemas; canonicalization preserves the array verbatim.

values.description: Ordered tuple: PostgreSQL compares enum values by declaration order.

kind.description: extension-*: owned by an installed extension. unsupported-*: a catalog structure this contract cannot yet represent faithfully.

reason.description: Why the object is opaque. Human-facing, part of the canonical form.
